{"arxiv_id":"2502.12638v2","arxiv_url":"http://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12638v2","title":"NExT-Mol: 3D Diffusion Meets 1D Language Modeling for 3D Molecule
  Generation","authors":["Zhiyuan Liu","Yanchen Luo","Han Huang","Enzhi Zhang","Sihang Li","Junfeng Fang","Yaorui Shi","Xiang Wang","Kenji Kawaguchi","Tat-Seng Chua"],"published_date":"2025-02-18T08:40:13Z","journal":"","doi":"","summary":"3D molecule generation is crucial for drug discovery and material design.
While prior efforts focus on 3D diffusion models for their benefits in modeling
continuous 3D conformers, they overlook the advantages of 1D SELFIES-based
Language Models (LMs), which can generate 100% valid molecules and leverage the
billion-scale 1D molecule datasets. To combine these advantages for 3D molecule
generation, we propose a foundation model -- NExT-Mol: 3D Diffusion Meets 1D
Language Modeling for 3D Molecule Generation. NExT-Mol uses an extensively
pretrained molecule LM for 1D molecule generation, and subsequently predicts
the generated molecule's 3D conformers with a 3D diffusion model. We enhance
NExT-Mol's performance by scaling up the LM's model size, refining the
diffusion neural architecture, and applying 1D to 3D transfer learning.
Notably, our 1D molecule LM significantly outperforms baselines in
distributional similarity while ensuring validity, and our 3D diffusion model
achieves leading performances in conformer prediction. Given these improvements
in 1D and 3D modeling, NExT-Mol achieves a 26% relative improvement in 3D FCD
for de novo 3D generation on GEOM-DRUGS, and a 13% average relative gain for
conditional 3D generation on QM9-2014. Our codes and pretrained checkpoints are
available at https://github.com/acharkq/NExT-Mol.","github_url":"https://github.com/acharkq/NExT-Mol","main_contributions":"The paper introduces NExT-Mol, a foundation model for 3D molecule generation that combines the strengths of 1D SELFIES-based Language Models (LMs) and 3D diffusion models. Key contributions include a novel diffusion model (DMT), a large-scale pretraining of a molecular LM (MoLlama), and a transfer learning approach to leverage 1D molecular representations for improved 3D conformer prediction. NExT-Mol achieves state-of-the-art performance in de novo 3D molecule generation, conditional 3D molecule generation, and 3D conformer prediction.","methodology":"NExT-Mol employs a two-step approach: first, generating a 1D molecule sequence using a pretrained MoLlama LM, and then predicting its 3D conformer with a Diffusion Molecular Transformer (DMT). The DMT model uses Relational Multi-Head Self-Attention (RMHA) and adaptive layernorm (adaLN) to incorporate 2D molecular graph information. Transfer learning is used to transfer MoLlama's 1D representations to DMT via a cross-modal projector.","experimental_setup":"The model is evaluated on the GEOM-DRUGS, GEOM-QM9, and QM9-2014 datasets. Performance is assessed using metrics such as FCD, atom stability, molecular stability, geometric similarity (bond lengths, bond angles, dihedral angles), Coverage (COV), and Average Minimum RMSD (AMR). Baselines include CDGS, JODO, MiDi, G-SchNet, G-SphereNet, EDM, MDM, GeoLDM, EEGSDE, EQGAT-diff, MolGPT, MolGen, OMEGA, GeoMol, GeoDiff, Torsional Diffusion, Particle Guidance, and MCF.","limitations":"The paper acknowledges limitations such as the performance drop on test molecules with unseen scaffolds, the lack of randomized SELFIES augmentation during pretraining, the causal self-attention in MoLlama, and the quadratic memory complexity of DMT's pair representation. The computational cost of incorporating MoLlama for 3D conformer prediction is also a limitation.","future_research_directions":"Future research directions include exploring advanced generalization techniques for unseen scaffolds, using randomized SELFIES augmentation in pretraining, using a molecular LM with built-in bi-directional self-attention, extending NExT-Mol to structure-based molecule generation, exploring diffusion guidance methods, and building multi-modal foundation models with NExT-Mol as the backbone for tasks like chemical reaction prediction and drug-drug interaction prediction."}

{"arxiv_id":"2312.07586v5","arxiv_url":"http://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07586v5","title":"Characteristic Guidance: Non-linear Correction for Diffusion Model at
  Large Guidance Scale","authors":["Candi Zheng","Yuan Lan"],"published_date":"2023-12-11T02:40:40Z","journal":"","doi":"","summary":"Popular guidance for denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) linearly
combines distinct conditional models together to provide enhanced control over
samples. However, this approach overlooks nonlinear effects that become
significant when guidance scale is large. To address this issue, we propose
characteristic guidance, a guidance method that provides first-principle
non-linear correction for classifier-free guidance. Such correction forces the
guided DDPMs to respect the Fokker-Planck (FP) equation of diffusion process,
in a way that is training-free and compatible with existing sampling methods.
Experiments show that characteristic guidance enhances semantic characteristics
of prompts and mitigate irregularities in image generation, proving effective
in diverse applications ranging from simulating magnet phase transitions to
latent space sampling.","github_url":"https://github.com/coderpiaobozhe/classifier-free-diffusion-guidance-Pytorch","main_contributions":"The paper introduces 'characteristic guidance,' a novel non-linear correction method for classifier-free guidance in denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs). It addresses the issue of image irregularities and semantic inconsistencies that arise at large guidance scales by enforcing adherence to the Fokker-Planck equation. The method is training-free and compatible with existing sampling techniques, improving image quality and semantic accuracy across various applications.","methodology":"The core of characteristic guidance involves a non-linear correction term added to the standard classifier-free guidance. This correction is derived from solving the score Fokker-Planck equation using the method of characteristics under the 'Harmonic ansatz,' which assumes the optimal DDPM solution is harmonic. The correction term is computed through a fixed-point iteration method, with acceleration algorithms for efficiency. Orthogonal projection operators are used as regularization to improve computation.","experimental_setup":"The method was evaluated on several tasks: modeling conditional Gaussian distributions, simulating magnet phase transitions using the Landau-Ginzburg model, and image generation using CIFAR-10, ImageNet 256, and Stable Diffusion. Image quality was assessed using metrics such as Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), and visual inspection. The experiments compared characteristic guidance against classifier-free guidance, demonstrating improvements in semantic characteristics and reduced irregularities.","limitations":"The effectiveness of FID as an evaluation metric for guided DDPMs is questioned due to the discrepancy between the target conditional probabilities and marginal probabilities. The iterative computation required for the non-linear correction can be slow, and the method's performance relies on the 'Harmonic ansatz,' which may not hold in all scenarios.","future_research_directions":"Future research directions include exploring advanced regularization techniques beyond projection to enhance the convergence rate and accelerate computation. Additionally, the paper suggests the need for developing more appropriate evaluation metrics better suited for assessing guided DDPMs. Further investigation is warranted to explore scenarios where the 'Harmonic ansatz' may not hold and to develop alternative methodologies."}
new_method:
New Method (Step 3): “Localized Characteristic Guidance for 3D Molecule Generation” (LCG-3DM)

Summary of Key Ideas:
• Introduce non-linear “characteristic guidance” within NExT-Mol’s 3D diffusion step, allowing dynamic, region-specific guidance for substructures (e.g., functional groups).  
• Enable adaptive scaling of the diffusion guidance so that previously unseen scaffolds are regularized by localized constraints, helping mitigate performance drops on out-of-distribution structures.  
• Maintain the advantages of NExT-Mol’s transfer learning from 1D LM to 3D diffusion while incorporating the characteristic correction concept to ensure stability and semantic consistency at large guidance scales.

Technical Highlights:

1) Regional Characteristic Guidance:  
   • Partition each molecule into meaningful substructures (e.g., ring systems, linkers, functional groups).  
   • During 3D diffusion, apply the characteristic guidance correction only to local gradient updates for each substructure, rather than a single global correction.  
   • This local guidance enforces the non-linear consistency prescribed by the Fokker–Planck constraints, ensuring that each substructure’s geometry remains coherent when scaling up the guidance intensity.  

2) Adaptive Guidance Scale Estimation:  
   • Dynamically assign guidance scales to each substructure based on its cumulative generation uncertainty (e.g., measured via local curvature in the conformer space or a substructure validity score).  
   • Higher risk of misalignment/out-of-distribution geometry triggers a larger local guidance correction; well-known motifs receive less.  
   • By localizing the guidance scale, LCG-3DM reduces the memory overhead and computational cost typically incurred by applying large uniform guidance everywhere.  

3) Cross-Modal Consistency Checks:  
   • Leverage the pretrained 1D MoLlama representations to identify whether a candidate local region (e.g., a substructure) is conforming to typical functional-group geometry.  
   • If mismatch is detected, the substructure’s intermediate diffusion step can re-inject local constraints via the characteristic guidance correction.  
   • This cross-modal synergy marries the 1D language model’s robust chemical prior with non-linear corrections in the 3D domain.  

Advantages Over Base Method:  
• Maintains high validity and distributional similarity benefits from the 1D LM.  
• Improves generalization on novel molecular scaffolds by treating substructures independently with localized non-linear guidance.  
• Lowers computational overhead compared to a naive global high-scale guidance, since only localized corrections are large-scale.  

In sum, LCG-3DM employs the core NExT-Mol idea of sequential 1D-to-3D generation but augments the diffusion step with substructure-specific characteristic guidance. By doing so, it addresses the Base Method’s noted challenge of performance drop on unseen scaffolds and enhances conformer quality at large guidance scales without suffering the pitfalls of uniform linear guidance.
